title: Compute a thick-core or uniformly bounded-coordinate dichotomy without saturation
statement: For templates (s,a+u) <-> (t,b+u) on Q x N^k, let F=Q[X_1,...,X_k]^Q and N=<e_s X^a-e_t X^b>. Monomial-vector differences belong to N exactly when the corresponding population states communicate. Put p=product X_i, J=N+p^T F and M=F/J. Since p^T M=0, finite primary decomposition yields a finite K with intersection_i X_i^K M=0, hence intersection_i(N+X_i^K F) subset N+p^T F. Enumerate K using exact Groebner module intersections and inclusion; the proof establishes termination. If a class can attain x_i >= K for each coordinate separately, every representative belongs to the intersection and therefore has an equivalent monomial divisible by p^T: an actual thick-core state. Otherwise one coordinate remains below K throughout the entire class. Encode that bounded coordinate in finite control and recurse. K is uniform in V and the class; recursion has depth at most d. No saturated lattice fibre replaces an actual class.
